# Iddhipādavibhaṅga (Vb 9)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Iddhipādavibhaṅga* is the ninth chapter of the *Vibhaṅga*, the second book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Hazra 1994]. The treatise is devoted to the systemic doctrinal and Abhidhammic analysis of the four "bases for spiritual power" or "roads to power" (*iddhipāda*): intention (*chanda*), energy (*viriya*), consciousness (*citta*), and investigation (*vīmaṁsā*), each coupled with concentration and volitional effort (*chanda-, viriya-, citta-, vīmaṁsa-samādhi-ppadhānasaṅkhāra-samannāgato iddhipādo*) [Gethin 2001; Nyanatiloka 1938]. Following the standard method of the *Vibhaṅga*, the chapter is organized into three distinct sections: the Sutta analysis (*sutta-bhājaniya*), the Abhidhamma analysis (*abhidhamma-bhājaniya*), and a catechetical interrogation (*pañhapucchaka*) [Hazra 1994; Nyanatiloka 1938].
In the *sutta-bhājaniya*, the text presents the standard canonical formula for the four *iddhipāda*s and breaks down its component phrases, offering definitions that are nearly identical with those preserved in the thirteenth discourse of the *Iddhipāda Saṁyutta* (SN 51.13) [Nyanatiloka 1938]. Within this section, the component of volitional strivings (*padhānasaṅkhāra*) is explained by means of the four right efforts (*sammappadhāna*) [Gethin 2001]. The *abhidhamma-bhājaniya* demonstrates the operation of the four factors at the level of supramundane absorption and skilful consciousness (*lokuttara-kusala-citta*) [Gethin 2001; Nyanatiloka 1938]. In its concluding portion, known as the *uttara-cūḷa-bhājaniya*, each factor alone (e.g., *chanda* or *viriya*) is strictly designated as the base of success (*iddhipāda*), while the associated mental aggregates are classified as conjoined with it [Gethin 2001]. In the *pañhapucchaka*, the *iddhipāda*s are examined under Abhidhamma matrix headings: they are determined to be wholly wholesome (*kusala*) and proper to disciples in higher training (*sekha*); investigation (*vīmaṁsā*, identified as non-delusion or *amoha*) functions as a root cause (*hetu*), whereas the other three factors do not [Nyanatiloka 1938].
Text-reuse computations demonstrate that the *Iddhipādavibhaṅga* shares substantial blocks of text with other chapters of the *Vibhaṅga*, particularly the *Sammappadhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 8), *Maggaṅgavibhaṅga* (Vb 11), *Saccavibhaṅga* (Vb 4), and *Jhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 12), as well as direct doctrinal parallels with the *Iddhipāda Saṁyutta* (SN 51) and the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language algorithmic alignments connect its formulas with parallel expositions of the *ṛddhipāda*s in Sanskrit and Tibetan scholastic literature, including the *Śrāvakabhūmi* of the *Yogācārabhūmi*, the *Arthaviniścayasūtra* (along with Vīryaśrīdatta's *Nibandhana*), Śamathadeva's *Abhidharmakośopāyikā*, and Chinese Āgama texts such as the *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
